resources.string: Getting started and pairing
AirTAK helps you find your teammates and share messages and markers during an airsoft game. Your phone or tablet talks to the radio over BLE; the radio carries traffic over the LoRa mesh.
Pair a device
Power on your compatible AirTAK radio and tap the link chip at the top of the app. Grant Bluetooth and location permissions when asked, then scan and select your radio.
Check the pairing code
Compare the six-digit code on the radio\'s e-ink display with the Android pairing prompt. Confirm only if both codes match.
Disconnect and reconnect
Disconnect drops the current link but keeps the radio remembered. Reconnect tries that radio again; Forget removes the saved pairing so you can start over.
Before you join the game
Set your callsign under Config > Player and use the same radio and channel setup as your teammates. Download the field\'s map and routing data while you still have internet access.
Offline use
Downloaded maps and radio traffic do not need mobile internet during play. Location searches, downloads and new map imagery may still need an internet connection.
Map and navigation
Use the map to see positions, shared markers and your planned route. A player\'s last reported position may be old, so check the roster before assuming they are still there.
Search
Find a town, place or coordinate and move the map there. Use this to find your field before downloading its map.
Add marker
Choose the kind of marker to draw, then tap the map to place its points. Undo removes the last point, Commit opens its details, and Send shares it with the selected audience.
Pause and resume
Pause marks your own game activity as inactive; resume makes it active again. This does not pause the game for everyone else.
Player status
Tap your status to report Active, HIT, RESPAWNING or ELIMINATED as appropriate. These reports inform other players; the app does not enforce the site\'s game rules.
Players button
Show or hide player positions on the map. This changes your map view, not whether those players can send updates.
Waypoints button
Show or hide waypoint markers on the map. Open the Markers tab when you want to search, inspect or locate a particular shared marker.
Imagery
Import an image of the field or mission plan and align it with the map. Adjust its corners and opacity; sharing alignment sends its placement, so another player still needs the matching image file.
Download tiles
Tap two corners to select an area, check the zoom range and tile URL, then download its map tiles. Download a manageable area before leaving internet coverage.
Layers button
This button selects an area for downloading BRouter routing data, not a list of map layers. Download these files if you want routes that follow roads and trails offline.
Plan route

Tap a start point and an end point to calculate a route. Without the required routing data, the app falls back to a straight line; a route is not a guarantee that access is allowed or the ground is safe.
Routing profile
Tap the profile chip to choose how a route is calculated. Pick the profile that suits how you plan to move, then check the resulting route against the field\'s rules.
Recenter
Return the map to your own position after looking elsewhere. A usable GPS position must be available first.
Map tab
Return to the field map and its drawing and route tools.
Net tab
Read and send radio messages without leaving the app.
Roster tab
Find players, inspect their latest reports and open actions such as Message or Locate.
Markers tab
Browse the shared points, routes, areas and objectives you have received.
Config tab
Change your identity, radio, channels and app preferences. Use Help here when you need a reminder during setup.
Link and HUD readings
The top bar helps you check whether the app has a radio link and recent device information. Missing readings are not the same as a zero reading.
No link
The app is not currently connected to its radio over BLE. Tap this chip to open device pairing or reconnect; being linked to a radio does not prove that another player is within mesh reach.
BAT
Check the battery level reported by your radio. It is not your phone\'s battery level.
GPS
Check satellite or fix information from the selected position source. If no fix is available, give the receiver a clearer view of the sky and check Position & Power.
RSSI
Check the reported received signal strength in dBm. A value closer to zero is stronger, but this reading is not a distance measurement or a guarantee of delivery across the mesh.
DC
Check the radio\'s duty-cycle load and warning level. High load can delay transmissions or cause relays to be dropped; reduce unnecessary traffic rather than bypassing the radio limits.
Net and messages
Net keeps channel conversations separate from direct messages. Messages travel over the radio mesh, so delivery depends on radio coverage and available airtime.
Mesh
Use the primary shared channel for traffic intended for the wider mesh, including compatible Meshtastic users. Treat an open channel as public.
Game
Use the secondary AirTAK channel for game coordination. Its name can differ if your group has renamed the channel.
Other channel tabs
Enabled channel slots appear as tabs. Select the slot used by your unit and check whether it is open or encrypted before sending.
Direct
Choose a heard node to open a conversation addressed to that player rather than the whole channel. The mesh may relay the message along the way; private addressing is not a promise of delivery.
Message scope
Choose All players or a unit level to set the intended audience. Set up your unit hierarchy and matching channels with your team before relying on scoped traffic.
Write and send
Type your message and tap Send. Keep it short so it takes less radio airtime.
Byte counter
The counter measures UTF-8 bytes against the 237-byte limit, not letters. Accents and other non-ASCII characters can use more than one byte.
Refresh
Request a sync of messages and markers when you think your local view is missing information. It cannot recover data that no reachable radio has available.
Roster
The roster shows players heard on the mesh, their units and their latest reports. An old report does not prove a player is still in the same place or status.
Search and filters
Search a callsign or unit to find a teammate. Use the available filters to narrow the list rather than scrolling through everyone.
Player details
Open a player to inspect their status and available position and radio information. Check how old those reports are before using them to coordinate a move.
Message
Open a direct conversation with this player.
Locate
Move the map to the player\'s reported position. If no position is available, wait for an update.
Ping
Send a request to the player\'s radio to check whether it responds. A missing response can mean poor coverage, not that the player has left the field.
Get markers
Request markers from this player to fill gaps in your local marker list.
Vote-kick
Cast a vote at the selected scope. Three distinct voters at the same scope hide that player from the local interface for 24 hours; their radio packets still pass through the mesh.
Markers
Markers let you share a place, route, area or objective without typing coordinates into chat. Their audience, team and priority help your group decide what each marker means.
Search and filters
Search labels and narrow the list by type or scope. Clear all filters if a marker seems to be missing.
Request markers
Request an update from all players or a particular heard node. This is useful after reconnecting or joining a game late.
Open and locate
Inspect a marker\'s description, creator, team and priority, then locate it on the map. Navigate calculates a route toward it using your selected routing profile.
Create and edit
Use the map\'s add-marker tool to place a point or draw a route or area. Set a clear label and the intended visibility before sending; edit controls are available for markers you own.
Objective
Use an objective marker to show a game location and its controlling team. Agree on its meaning with the marshals; it does not automatically award points or enforce capture rules.
Delete
Deleting a marker you own broadcasts a removal record so other players can remove their copies too. Players outside radio reach may not see that change immediately.
Config sections
Read loads the current group of settings from the radio. Apply sends your edits to it; changing radio settings can briefly interrupt LoRa reception while BLE stays connected.
Player
Set your callsign, device names and map colour. Add optional Fireteam, Squad, Platoon and Company names and link each unit level to its agreed channel.
Device HIT button
Enable the HIT toggle if you want a long press on the radio\'s user button to report a hit. Make sure you know which button and gesture your hardware uses before the game starts.
LoRa Radio
Choose the legal region, TX power and PHY profiles for your site. Coordinate these with your team; incompatible profiles can prevent radios hearing each other.
Channels
Manage eight slots and their PSKs or shared passwords. Slots 0 and 1 provide the shared and game channels, slot 2 is reserved for future audio, and slots 3 to 7 can carry unit traffic.
Matching channel settings
Teammates need matching slot, name and password settings for the intended unit channel. A blank password makes a channel open; use an agreed encrypted channel for position sharing.
Position & Power
Choose phone GPS or the radio\'s GPS, the position channel and broadcast timing. Smart beaconing adjusts position reports; shorter intervals use more airtime and power.
Power controls
Adjust the available display timeout and brightness settings. The GPS duty-cycle control is marked for a later development phase, so do not depend on it for battery savings yet.
Security
Set the allowed BLE bond count for the radio. This controls remembered Bluetooth pairings, not who shares your mesh channel password.
Moderation
Review active vote-kick bans, their scopes and expiry. Unban restores a hidden player in your local view; it does not remove their radio from the mesh.
Application
Choose your theme and optional map tile server. The tile URL needs the server\'s zoom and coordinate placeholders; use a source you are allowed to download from.
Language
Choose English, German or the system default for the app\'s labels. Changing language rebuilds the screens and closes the view you had open.
Help
Open this guide when you need to check a control or prepare the app for a game.
Share Config
Export a QR setup for teammates or scan one and review its summary before applying it. A shared setup can contain channel secrets, so show it only to people who should join your group.
About
Inspect diagnostics, restart the radio or reboot the device when troubleshooting. Open Update Firmware here; factory reset is marked as a later feature, not a working recovery button.
Battery Optimization
Open Android\'s battery settings if background restrictions keep interrupting your connection. Android controls this setting, so its wording can vary between devices.
Firmware updates
Firmware runs on the radio, not in the Android app. Update it with a file intended for your exact device and board revision.
Choose a file
Open Config > About > Update Firmware and select the appropriate .bin or .zip package. Do not flash a file for different hardware just because its name looks similar.
Update via Bluetooth
Use BLE when the radio is paired and nearby. Keep it powered and within range throughout transfer, verification and restart.
Update via USB cable
Connect the radio with a data-capable USB cable and use the USB update option. Grant Android access to the USB device if prompted.
Progress and verification
Wait while the app transfers and verifies the image, then let the radio restart. Do not unplug it or switch it off during the update.
Failure and logs
If the update fails, read the error and debug log before retrying. Check the file, power and connection rather than repeatedly flashing an unknown image.
